title: Meridian Freight / Halden Logistics - Negotiation Call

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: Thanks for hopping back on. Since we last spoke, Yuki confirmed the Freightline integration is doable with a moderate custom connector, not a heavy lift.

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: Right - Freightline exposes a documented API, just not one we'd pre-built. I'm estimating three weeks of integration work, which still fits inside your two-month target alongside the carrier onboarding.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: That's good news. What would that custom connector cost on top of your standard pricing?

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: We'd typically charge a one-time integration fee for custom connectors - for this scope I can offer $12,000, which is discounted from our usual $18,000 rate as a new-customer incentive.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: We were hoping to stay under $10,000 for one-time fees given this is a one-year pilot commitment, not a multi-year deal.

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: I can go to $10,000 if we agree to a two-year term instead of evaluating year to year - that gives us the volume to justify the discount.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: Let me think about the two-year term - I'd need to check budget approval for that, since one-year was already approved.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Separately, can the custom connector be reused if we later add a second facility on Freightline?

transcript.speaker: Yuki Tanaka
transcript.text: Yes, the connector's designed at the account level, not per-facility, so a second facility would just need additional configuration, not new development.

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: Good to confirm. Linda, when do you expect to know on the two-year term?

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: I should have an answer by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: Great, let's plan to finalize pricing and get a contract over by early next week assuming Friday goes well.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: One last open question from our side - what does onboarding support look like in the first month after go-live? Is there dedicated support, or standard tickets only?

transcript.speaker: Carlos Reyes
transcript.text: For a deal this size we'd include a dedicated onboarding specialist for the first 30 days. I'll put that in writing in the contract.

transcript.speaker: Linda Park
transcript.text: That helps, thank you. Talk Friday.

summary_key_points: The Freightline integration is confirmed feasible with about three weeks of custom connector work
Pricing negotiation centers on a one-time integration fee, discounted to $10,000 if Halden commits to a two-year term
Halden needs budget approval for a two-year term, expected by Friday
Meridian will include a dedicated onboarding specialist for the first 30 days after go-live

action_items.task: Get budget approval for a two-year term and respond by Friday
Prepare the contract with the discounted integration fee and dedicated onboarding support, pending Friday's answer

decisions: Offer Halden a $10,000 discounted integration fee in exchange for a two-year term instead of one-year
Include a dedicated onboarding specialist for Halden's first 30 days after go-live
open_questions: Will Halden commit to a two-year term to unlock the discounted integration fee, and will they confirm by Friday?
